nuggets.title: Gang Scheduling Deadlock Leaves 80 GPUs Idle

scenario.symptoms: Cluster shows 80 free GPUs while 15 large training jobs stay pending for 6 hours. Each job needs 8 GPUs simultaneously but cluster fragments into 7-GPU islands.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Scheduler allocates GPUs one at a time without gang scheduling or backfill; partial placements never start.

incident.headline: Non-gang GPU scheduling fragments cluster and deadlocks large distributed training jobs

agenda.goal: Schedule multi-GPU jobs with gang/all-or-nothing placement, queueing, and optional backfill policies.
agenda.opener: We had free GPUs but big training jobs never started. How does your platform schedule jobs that need 8 GPUs at once?

evidence.strong: Gang scheduler with minAvailable, coscheduling plugin, reservation pools, preemption rules, topology-aware placement on same NVLink domain.

misconceptions.pattern: Equates cluster utilization with successful job starts.
misconceptions.challenge: If seven GPUs are free on seven nodes, can an 8-GPU job run?

probes: When do you preempt smaller jobs?
agenda.referenceFix: Gang scheduling with queue, topology constraints, preemption for small jobs when configured.

nuggets.title: Partial Checkpoint Write Corrupts Week-Long Training Run

scenario.symptoms: Job resumed from checkpoint after node failure diverges immediately with NaN loss. Object store contains truncated shard files from crash mid-upload.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Checkpoints written directly to shared bucket without atomic rename or step validation on resume.

incident.headline: Non-atomic checkpoint persistence serves corrupted state after worker failure

agenda.goal: Write checkpoints atomically with step metadata, keep last N good checkpoints, validate on resume.
agenda.opener: Resuming from checkpoint after a node death produced NaNs. How do you checkpoint long training jobs safely?

evidence.strong: Write to temp prefix then commit pointer, fsync/complete multipart, store step and hash manifest, resume validates before delete old, frequent incremental checkpoints.

misconceptions.pattern: Assumes less frequent checkpoints are always cheaper overall.
misconceptions.challenge: What is the cost of restarting a 7-day run from scratch?

probes: How do you detect a bad checkpoint before training continues?
Where is the pointer to latest good step?
agenda.referenceFix: Atomic checkpoint commits, manifest with step id, validation on load, retain last two steps.

nuggets.title: Shared NFS Metadata Storm Slows All Jobs

scenario.symptoms: Input pipeline stalls; GPU utilization drops to 30% cluster-wide. NFS metadata ops/sec peg while thousands of workers list same dataset directory.
scenario.interviewerSetup: All training jobs read shards via POSIX on shared NFS with small files per sample instead of object store or localized cache.

incident.headline: POSIX metadata bottleneck on shared filesystem starves GPU training pipelines

agenda.goal: Serve training data from object storage with shard manifests, local NVMe cache, and sequential read patterns.
agenda.opener: GPUs sit idle while NFS melts from dataloader metadata ops. Where should training data live and how is it read?

evidence.strong: Parquet/WebDataset shards on object storage, node-local cache, prefetch pipeline, manifest files not per-file listing, high-throughput parallel reads.
evidence.weak: Millions of small files on NFS.

misconceptions.pattern: Treats shared POSIX as scalable data lake for ML.
misconceptions.challenge: What happens when 2000 workers stat the same directory?

probes: How are shards assigned to workers?
When do you cache locally on GPU nodes?
hints: Sequential large objects beat random small files.
agenda.referenceFix: Object store + shard format, local cache on training nodes, dataloader prefetch tuned to GPU.

nuggets.title: Production Model Deployed Without Dataset Version Trace

scenario.symptoms: Regulator asks which training snapshot produced model v3.2; team cannot reproduce metrics because dataset was overwritten in place with same path.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Jobs log git commit but not immutable dataset snapshot id; data team updated labels under s3://training/latest/ without bumping version.

incident.headline: Missing immutable dataset lineage prevents reproducing or auditing trained models

agenda.goal: Capture end-to-end lineage: code, data snapshot, hyperparameters, metrics, and artifacts with immutable ids.
agenda.opener: We cannot prove which data trained model v3.2 after the dataset path was overwritten. What lineage do you record per job?

evidence.strong: Immutable dataset snapshots with content hash, MLflow/W&B run ids linked to registry, config as code, artifact signing, block promote without lineage fields.

misconceptions.challenge: If data at the path changes tomorrow, what trained yesterday?

probes: What must be immutable before training starts?
How does registry block incomplete lineage?
agenda.referenceFix: Versioned dataset snapshots, mandatory lineage metadata on model promotion.

nuggets.title: Single Straggler GPU Kills Distributed Training Step

scenario.symptoms: 128-GPU job hangs every 20 minutes at all-reduce; NCCL timeouts fire after one worker on a noisy network link slows collective.
scenario.interviewerSetup: No automatic straggler detection or elastic shrink; job fails entirely on NCCL timeout instead of isolating bad node.

incident.headline: Network straggler on one GPU node stalls entire synchronous distributed training step

agenda.goal: Handle slow/failed nodes with health checks, elastic training, backup communicators, and automatic replace.
agenda.opener: One bad network link hung our 128-GPU job repeatedly. How does the platform handle failures during distributed training?

evidence.strong: Node health preflight, NCCL async error handling, elastic/deep speed restart, exclude bad nodes, RDMA/network topology placement, checkpoint resume on shrink.

misconceptions.pattern: Assumes GPU count alone defines training reliability.
misconceptions.challenge: What happens to all-reduce if one participant is 10x slower?

probes: When do you shrink world size vs restart?
How fast can you replace a bad node?
agenda.referenceFix: Straggler detection, automatic node replacement, elastic resume from checkpoint with smaller world size.
